title: Bankrupt, legally free, and he paid anyway

lines.text: Bankrupt, legally off the hook, and he paid his debts anyway.
Pittsburgh, 1875. Henry Heinz's first food company collapsed.
It owed far more than it owned.
Bankruptcy wiped the slate clean. Legally, he owed nobody a cent.
In 1876 he started again, with his brother and his cousin.
But he kept his old creditors in mind, and he paid them back.
By 1888 the company carried his name: H. J. Heinz.
So what would you do, if you were bankrupt and legally off the hook?
